commitResults.messageTitle: Setup and implement Level 0: rename chatbot, greet and exit
Add command echoing for Level 1, read commands until bye to support a basic interactive session.
Add Level 2 task storage and listing
Update gitignore, implement step 1 and 2 of Level-3, mark and unmark
Implement step 2 of Level-3: create and refactor tasks into a Task class
Implement step 1 of Level 4, add support for tracking three types of tasks (without Level 4 extension)
Implement step 2 of Level 4: implement A-Inheritance extension
Implement Level 5: Handle errors with A-Exceptions extension
Implement Level 6 (delete) and implement A-Collections extension
Save task list after each change
commitResults.messageBody:
Task updates exist only in memory, so they are lost when Koara exits.

Write the complete task list to a relative data file after each change.
Store task details in a format that can be loaded in the next increment.

Clean up the existing Java code to follow the course coding standard.
Add package organization, API documentation, and compliant wrapping.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load saved tasks when Koara starts
commitResults.messageBody:
Koara saves task changes to disk but currently starts with an empty
task list.

Load all task types and their completion status from the relative data
file. Create the data directory when needed and handle invalid or
inaccessible data without crashing.

Run each UI test in an isolated folder so saved tasks do not leak
between test cases.

Deadline and event dates are stored as raw text, so Koara cannot
validate or interpret them.

Store dates as LocalDate values, accept the yyyy-MM-dd input format,
and display them as MMM dd yyyy. Preserve ISO dates in the data file so
saved tasks can be loaded reliably.

Update UI tests to cover valid and invalid date input.

Koara handles user interaction, command parsing, task management, and
file storage in one class, making its responsibilities difficult to
follow and change independently.

Extract Ui, Parser, TaskList, and Storage classes for those concerns.
Keep Koara as the application coordinator while preserving existing
behavior and data compatibility.

All classes currently share the koara package, making unrelated
responsibilities harder to locate as the project grows.

Group task, UI, storage, parser, and exception classes into focused
subpackages. Keep src/main/java as the source root and Koara as the
application entry point.

Core parsing, task-list, and storage behavior currently relies on
manual testing, making regressions difficult to detect.

Add tests for valid and invalid parsing, task-list operations and
serialization, and storage save/load behavior.

The Shadow task still uses the starter Duke filename, which does not
match the application being distributed.

Configure the fat JAR as koara.jar so users can identify and run the
packaged application with java -jar.

Some overridden and internal methods still lack documentation for
their behavior, parameters, return values, and errors.

Document all remaining non-private methods and non-trivial private
methods, including command execution, storage parsing, and date
validation.

Several identifiers do not clearly describe their purpose or follow
the required verb and collection naming conventions.

Rename task-list sizing, date fields, UI constants, and test
collections to make their roles explicit while preserving behavior.

Users cannot locate tasks without scanning the full list manually.

Add a find command that validates its keyword, searches task
descriptions, and displays matching tasks in their original order.
Cover valid, empty, matching, and non-matching cases with JUnit tests.
